one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) Intuitive Q3 2026 results on Oct 20 after the close (consensus non-GAAP EPS ~$2.54-2.64; the $2.13 figure in some previews is GAAP), where management has promised to quantify the 2027 Extended Use Program (said at the Sept 9 Wells Fargo conference) and will likely frame 2027; (2) possible FDA clearance of Medtronic Hugo for U.S. general surgery/gynecology, which Medtronic said to expect 'this fall' (510(k)s filed June 3), a modest headline negative; (3) HCA/Tenet Q3 prints in late October giving the read on ACA-driven elective deferral. Industry evidence says Q3 U.S. da Vinci growth stays near Q2's 12% or dips slightly: HCA's elective inpatient surgery was -6% in Q2 and its CFO reaffirmed the slowdown on Sept 15; Tenet expects exchange-to-uninsured conversion to continue through H2; an Evercore ISI survey (Sept 23) found 24% of hospital executives already seeing slower procedures and 56% expecting it within 6-12 months. Offsetting: OUS (~19%) and da Vinci 5 trade-ins should keep placements firm, the stock already trades ~33x 2027 EPS after a ~30% YTD fall, and the 2020 EUP precedent (modeled -7%, actual -2% revenue per procedure) suggests the EUP number may be less bad than feared. Net: two-sided risk, no edge. I use a lognormal with median ~$402.5 and an 11.5% one-month sigma (above the 37%/3.5 = 10.6% baseline for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY2028 non-GAAP EPS est. $13.70 x 33x = $452, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (FY2028 FCF/share est. $13.55 / 3.0% = $452, weight 0.4), valued as of Oct 2027; FY2027 EPS haircut ~2% to consensus (smaller than round 1) for ACA deferral, China and the Extended Use Program.

Stock at ~33x consensus FY2027 EPS ($401.24/$12.20). I hold that multiple: competitive entry is real but early (Ottava launching only at select institutions with more trials over 12-18 months; Hugo US general surgery clearance pending, ~250 units target globally vs 11,710 da Vinci), offset by ~12-14% EPS growth and $8.6B cash. Sell-side average PT ~$476 (32 analysts) implies ~37x on 2027 consensus, which I treat as evidence that 33x is not aggressive.

bear.story: U.S. procedure growth slides toward ~10% as ACA coverage losses persist (subsidy restoration unlikely per prediction markets; HCA/Tenet see exchange patients shifting one-for-one to uninsured), bariatric keeps shrinking, the EUP hit lands closer to the 7% originally modeled in 2020 than the 2% realized, China share keeps falling, and Hugo (general surgery clearance) and Ottava win early IDN deals; FY2028 EPS ~$12 at ~25x.

base.story: Procedure growth ~12-14% with ACA comps lapping in 2027, da Vinci 5 trade-ins (144 in Q2 vs 83) and ASC XiR sustain capital, EUP costs ~1-2% of revenue per procedure, competitors remain sub-scale through 2027; FY2028 EPS ~$13.7 at ~33x.

bull.story: Deferred benign procedures return, OUS growth ~19-20% persists, EUP drives incremental volume as in 2020-21, Ottava's select-institution launch and Hugo's general-surgery entry prove slow, Force Feedback CE mark widens the moat in Europe; multiple re-rates toward ~40x on ~$14 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$300 the stock would trade at ~22x my FY2028 EPS and ~25x consensus FY2027 EPS, which only makes sense if procedure growth is structurally heading to single digits, competitors are taking meaningful U.S. soft-tissue share (Ottava multi-system IDN wins, Hugo winning general surgery after clearance), or instrument pricing erodes well beyond the Extended Use Program. The 52-week low of $328.57 was set on sentiment after the Q2 guide; a sustained break of ~$300 would signal a fundamental change rather than volatility.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with ~25 additional searches, mostly industry-lane. Customer side: HCA's Q2 same-facility inpatient surgeries -2.3% and outpatient -4.4% (Healthcare Dive), elective inpatient -6% (CFO at Jefferies, Sept 15); exchange admissions -15% and uninsured +15% (correcting my round-1 +23%); Tenet also sees one-for-one conversion continuing into H2; Evercore ISI's Sept 23 survey shows 24% of hospital execs seeing slower procedures and 56% expecting it within 6-12 months; prediction markets gave low odds of enhanced-subsidy restoration. So the ACA headwind persists through at least early 2027, consistent with Intuitive's Q2 U.S. growth of 12% and its Sept 9 commentary. Bariatric is now ~2% of global procedures (from 5%), so the GLP-1 drag is shrinking in weight. Pricing: the 2020 EUP precedent (modeled -7%, actual -2% revenue per procedure) and Goldman's ~-1%/yr model made my round-1 EUP haircut too large, so I cut my FY2027 haircut from ~3.5% to ~2% ($11.90 -> $12.00). Competition: Ottava is launching only with select leading institutions and J&J plans more trials over 12-18 months; Medtronic's Hugo targets ~250 installed units with general-surgery/gyn 510(k)s pending, and Medtronic also bought into Cornerstone Robotics for OUS; CMR is exploring a ~$4B sale. Competitive share loss remains a 2028+ earnings risk that caps the multiple rather than a 12-month driver. China: verified H1 2026 tenders, da Vinci 10 of 27 units (37% vs 62%), ASP -19%, MicroPort Toumai 300+ orders; small for the group. Capital: trade-ins 144 vs 83, ~half of U.S. placements, supports system revenue despite hospital capex caution. Valuation: $13.70 FY2028 EPS x 33x = $452, cross-checked with a 3% FCF yield on $13.55 FCF/share = $452 (H1 FCF verified at $1.76B from the 10-Q). Sell-side average PT ~$476 (32 analysts) is evidence, not the answer. Scenarios: bear $300 (26%), base $450 (51%), bull $590 (23%), mean ~$443. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals (sigmas 0.23/0.18/0.21), slightly wider than round 1 to bring the log-spread (~0.31) closer to the 37% realized vol; median ~$434, P(>=401)=0.60. One-month ladder is near-symmetric around $402.5 with an 11.5% sigma for the Oct 20 print.
